title: Core Scientific files for 285MW data center outside Dallas, Texas
html:
Core Scientific has filed to develop a new data center outside Dallas, Texas.

In a filing with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, Telios Quinlan One, LLC has filed for the Core Scientific - Hunt data center project.

The development, located some 53 miles northeast of Dallas at 4852 County Road 3507 in Quinlan, Hunt County, is described as a 341,325 sq ft (31,710 sqm) data center core and shell building.

Construction on the $1.3 billion project is set to run from November 2026 until September 2028.

The site, located close to Acciona Energia’s 190MW Cunningham battery energy storage system (BESS), is currently mostly vacant land.

Core Scientific first announced it had acquired a 265-acre site in Hunt County in March, buying Telios Quinlan One LLC for $232.5 million.

At the time the company said the campus could support up to 285MW of leasable capacity (430MW gross capacity) across multiple buildings, and the site could begin energizing in 2027, r,eaching full power by 2029. An on-site substation is planned.

AMD is set to lease 110MW in Hunt County from Core Scientific as part of a wider leasing agreement.

Renewable energy infrastructure developer Belltown Power was previously looking to develop a project in Quinlan, but withdrew its application earlier this year, according to a local anti-data center group.

Founded in 2017, Core Scientific began as a cryptomining data center operator, but has now pivoted to AI data center development. The company has facilities across Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, North Dakota, Oklahoma, and Texas. As well as AMD, AI cloud firm CoreWeave is a major customer.

This week, it announced it intends to fully exit its Bitcoin mining business by the end of the year, to focus on AI infrastructure.
summary: Company set to lease around half of site to AMD
